The proof problem

Everybody has to take your word for it.

The people choosing who gets the job. The people paying for it. The tradesperson deciding where to work next. Three different decisions, and not one of them is made by somebody who has seen you work.

The difference is out on your projects. It is in the call your PM made when the drawings were wrong. The problem you found before it became the owner's problem. The work you stood behind after the invoice was paid.

None of that leaves the site. We bring it back, and put it where the decision gets made.

  • Nothing to show. You have finished a dozen projects and the only record is photos on a superintendent's phone.
  • Deals stall after the quote. Your estimator sends the number and then waits. There is nothing to send on Thursday that is not a nudge.
  • Stakeholders in the dark. The owner is in another city reading a written report. He asks the same three questions every month.
  • Crews you cannot fill. You are short on every job and your careers page has a photo on it you bought from a website.

How it works

You introduce the people. We make it happen.

You are running a job, not a production. One agreed day on site captures the work as it stands; the interviews carry the story of the whole project.

01

We plan it before we film it.

We agree the story angle and the problems the content has to solve before a camera comes out of the case. Every deliverable is mapped to one of them.

02

Interviews tell the whole project.

A camera only sees the day it is there. The story of the whole job, from the drawings to the handover, comes from coordinated interviews with the people who ran it and the client it was built for.

03

The camera captures the agreed site day.

One agreed day on site. Access, permissions and releases are sorted first, and we bring cameras, insurance certificates and PPE. Brief interviews are arranged around the job: no staged performance, and no production management from your team.

04

Then we do the rest.

We edit, write and build the page, then hand it over with a short guide to using it in sales. You approve it once, in one place.

Your part

  • Introduce your project lead and the client or authorized site contact
  • Give brief interviews at agreed times
  • Confirm the permissions only you can give
  • Send one consolidated round of notes

Our part

  • Scheduling, calls and the shoot window
  • Story planning and interview direction
  • Filming, editing, writing and the page
  • The production timeline, from the first call to delivery

The deadline

A finished building is just a building.

The proof is the work, and the work only exists while it is happening. Once the site demobilizes, no version of this can be recovered. Not at any price, not by anyone.

If there is a job running right now that you would want a committee to see, that is the one.

The guarantee

The things we guarantee, in plain terms.

01

First cut in fourteen days, or you do not pay.

The first cut is the edited project film, complete enough to review: the story in order, with the interviews and the footage, before your revision round. The fourteen days start the day after the site day, or after the last coordinated interview if that comes later. The clock pauses only when we are waiting on a specific input that only you can give us, such as a signed release, and we name it when it happens. Our own editing and staffing never pause it. If the first cut is late, the project is free: anything you have paid is refunded in full and you keep every file.

02

Final delivery follows one round of notes.

You send one consolidated set of notes, gathered from everyone who needs a say. We make those changes and deliver the final film, the social cuts, the written case study, the page, the bid PDF and the stills. Final delivery has no fixed date because it depends on when your notes arrive; we confirm the date the day we receive them.

03

If the footage is not right, we come back on our dime.

If what we got does not hold up, we book another day and cover it. No change order, no mobilization fee.

Questions

A few things worth knowing.

Why the founding rate?

We are building a commercial construction portfolio. The founding rate is for three qualifying projects, with written agreement on which approved work we can feature, and for exactly the scope listed here.

Who qualifies?

A commercial contractor or trade with a Central Ohio project where meaningful work is visible; a real use for the story, such as an upcoming bid, a prequalification or a sales follow-up; one authorized contact who can introduce the people involved; and approval to film the site and feature the approved work. The project-fit call is where we confirm it together.

What happens on the project-fit call?

You tell us about the job. We tell you straight whether it is a fit, recommend a story angle, and set out exactly what would be filmed, who would be interviewed and what you would get. You leave with that whether or not you go ahead.

Do we have to manage the shoot?

No. You introduce the people and name the authorized site contact. We handle the scheduling and the production. Your team still gives the agreed interviews, the permissions only it can give, and one round of approval.

Does one day cover the whole project?

The camera covers one agreed day on site: the work as it stands, the crew, the details. The story of the whole project comes from the interviews, with the people who ran it and the client it was built for. Filming more than one stage or location is a separate scope.

Does the client need to appear on camera?

An approved client interview makes the story stronger, so we confirm availability before reserving the project. If the client declines, we build a fact-led project story that does not imply a client endorsement.

Is fourteen days the final delivery date?

No. Fourteen days is the first cut: the edited project film, complete enough to review, before your revision round. The social cuts, the written case study, the page, the bid PDF and the stills follow with final delivery, after your one consolidated round of notes. We confirm that date when the notes arrive.

When does the fourteen day clock start, and what pauses it?

It starts the day after the completed site day, or after the last coordinated interview if that is later. It pauses only when we are waiting on a specific input that only you can give us, such as a signed release, and we name it when it happens. Our own editing and staffing never pause it.

What happens if the first cut is late?

The project is free. Anything you have already paid is refunded in full, and you keep every file we have made.

What is a consolidated revision round?

One set of notes, gathered from everyone who needs a say, sent to us in one place. We make those changes and deliver the final files.

What if the site is confidential?

This founding group needs permission to share approved work, so a project that has to stay private is not a fit for the founding rate. Ask us about a separate private scope.

Do we own the files?

You receive the final outputs and your organized raw footage. Licensed music and any other third-party material follow their license terms.

Will this guarantee a won bid?

No. We make evidence your team can use in proposals and sales conversations. Whether a buyer chooses you still depends on your offer, qualifications, price and competition.

Can we add another location or a crew film?

Yes, by separate scope and price, agreed before work starts. The founding package covers one project and one location.

What about ongoing work?

We talk about it after the first story, once we both know it is a good fit. The founding package stands on its own.

What if the weather turns?

We reschedule at no charge and the clock starts from the new date.
